The Ohio Department of Natural Resources (ODNR) has selected Craig Watson to serve as Ohio’s Boating Law Administrator, where he will lead the state’s boating safety, education, and enforcement programs, while overseeing Ohio’s partnership with the U.S. Coast Guard and other national boating organizations.
p
Watson brings more than 20 years of experience with ODNR to the role, having dedicated his career to promoting safe and responsible boating throughout Ohio.
p

As Boating Law Administrator, Watson will lead Ohio’s boating law administration program, including statewide boating safety initiatives, education and training programs, enforcement priorities, grant management, and coordination with local, state, and federal partners. He will also serve as a liaison to the Waterways Safety Council and oversee Marine Patrol, Boating Education, and Equipment Loan grant programs that support boating communities across the state.
p

“Craig’s commitment to boating safety, education, and public service has made a lasting impact across Ohio,” said ODNR Director Mary Mertz. “His extensive experience, leadership, and passion for helping people safely enjoy Ohio’s waterways make him exceptionally well suited to lead the state’s boating law administration efforts.”
p

Watson previously served as a Natural Resources Administrator with ODNR’s Division of Parks and Watercraft, where he administered Ohio’s boating education grant program and coordinated statewide boating education training, programs, and events for Natural Resources Officers, park naturalists, and boating partners. He also managed the nationally verified Ohio Paddling Instructor Program.
p

“Ohio’s waterways provide outstanding opportunities for recreation, education, and conservation,” Watson said. “I am honored to take on this role and continue working with our partners across the state and nation to promote boating safety, strengthen education programs, and help ensure Ohio remains a great place to enjoy time on the water.”
p

A graduate of Columbus State Community College and Tiffin University, Watson began his career with the Ohio Division of Watercraft as a college intern in 1999 and was hired as a State Watercraft Officer in 2000. Following his promotion to Natural Resources Administrator in 2014, he assumed leadership of boating education initiatives across the state.
p

Throughout his career, Watson has earned recognition as an accomplished instructor and trainer. He serves as an instructor trainer for Marine Patrol, ODNR paddling courses, the Ohio Boating Education Course classroom program, and the National Safe Boating Council’s Boat Control Course. He is also a graduate of the 2019 National Association of State Boating Law Administrators (NASBLA) Leadership Academy and has played an active leadership role on NASBLA’s Paddle Sports Committee, serving as Charge Lead, Vice Chair, and Chair of the subcommittee for Paddle Sports within the Education Committee.
p

Ohio’s waterways support millions of recreational boating trips each year, and ODNR remains committed to providing the education, enforcement, and resources necessary to keep Ohioans and visitors safe while enjoying the state’s lakes, rivers, and streams.
p
For more information about boating safety, education courses, and Ohio boating regulations, visit the ODNR website.
p

Recognized as the No. 1 state park system in America with the 2025 National Gold Medal Award for Excellence in Park and Recreation Management, the ODNR Division of Parks and Watercraft provides exceptional outdoor recreation and boating opportunities by balancing outstanding customer service, education, and conservation of Ohio’s 76 state parks and waterways.
p
ODNR ensures a balance between wise use and protection of our natural resources for the benefit of all. Visit the ODNR website at ohiodnr.gov.
